reviewers.agent: two parallel general-purpose subagents on disjoint dimensions (9h1 shutdown / a9f resource), each with the engine:claude rule bodies, the review charter and its own memory recall
general-purpose subagent, sole arbiter over the union of both passes; settled the concurrency claim by building its own harness

three successive rounds (dacd766, 8587a84, fd7a015..HEAD), each verdicting the prior round's findings and hunting for defects the repair introduced; the last was an independent review of the final commit only

records.finding: The first fix's atomic.Bool guard narrowed the silent-drop window without closing it: providerSink.Shutdown did not take the lock emit holds, so a caller past the flag check could resume inside emit against a stopped provider, where sdklog discards the record and ForceFlush answers nil.
records.evidence: Examiner harness, 500 iterations of ExportEvents racing Shutdown: 12-13 silent drops per 500, 82/500 under -race, no data race. Production model over emit.Std's own Flush/Close ordering: 10/10 runs returned nil having delivered 1484-2048 of 6000 outcomes.
records.reason: The sink decides under the same slot emit holds: Shutdown marks stopped before waiting, emit reads it after taking the slot. Verified across forced interleavings by two independent passes; the regression test fails the previous fix at 35 of 300 races.

records.finding: Introduced by the first repair: waiting on a sync.Mutex made Shutdown uncancellable, so it overran its deadline behind an in-flight emit. One emitChunk is an OTLP HTTP export with its own timeout and retries.
records.evidence: Measured 280ms against a 10ms deadline where the pre-repair code returned in 12ms. emit/emitter.go documents that Close cancels in-flight work so it can honour its ctx.
records.reason: The sink serialises on a one-slot channel whose acquire selects against ctx.Done(). TestShutdownHonorsItsDeadline pins it and fails the mutex version at 280ms.

records.finding: Introduced by the second repair: on an abandoned wait, Shutdown called provider.Shutdown with an expired ctx while an emit still held the slot. sdklog latches stopped before honouring ctx, so the in-flight emit's remaining chunks were discarded and it returned nil — the same silent drop the series exists to close.
records.evidence: Reproduced at the public API: two-chunk batch, expired-ctx Shutdown, 'ExportEvents = <nil>, delivered = 2048 of 2053'. Reachable without a tight deadline because Exporter.Shutdown runs the metric leg first on the same ctx.
records.reason: Shutdown returns the ctx error without touching the provider when it cannot wait, so the in-flight batch lands. TestShutdownDeadlineNeverLosesEventsSilently fails the previous commit at 2048 of 2053. The final independent review could not produce a silent drop on any path it tried, under -race.

records.finding: acquire's two-case select picks at random when the slot is free and the ctx already expired, so about half of expired-ctx Shutdowns still handed the provider a dead deadline, stranding it latched-but-alive with every later Shutdown returning nil.
records.evidence: Reviewer measured 27/60 stranded, and 26/60 through the public API with a metric leg consuming the budget. My own test: 101 of 200 without the fix, 0 with it.
records.reason: acquire checks ctx.Err() before the select. TestExpiredCtxNeverStrandsTheProvider fails the unfixed version at 101 of 200.

records.finding: ErrShutdown is exported API sold by its doc as 'an error the caller can test for', but nothing pinned its identity; replacing both returns with a plain error left the suite green.
records.reason: Both assertions use errors.Is and fail that mutation.

records.finding: TestBothLegsResolveTheSameResource tested the helper rather than the shipping path: breaking what New passes to buildResourceMetrics or newProviderSink left the package green.
records.evidence: Both mutations applied together: 'ok ... 0.383s'. The wiring block only read struct fields, never what the export methods delivered.
records.reason: It exports through Exporter.ExportMetrics and pins that New hands both legs the same resource; providerSink keeps the resource it was built from so that is observable. Both mutations now fail.

records.finding: WithResource, the exported option whose precedence contract this change rewrote, had no test anywhere in the repo.
records.evidence: grep for WithResource excluding sdklog.WithResource returns only the doc comment and the declaration.
records.reason: TestWithResourceMergesRatherThanOverrides added, including the case defaultResource() cannot reach — a caller resource omitting service.name leaves it to OTEL_SERVICE_NAME. It fails a reversed merge order.

records.finding: The 'legs agree' assertion was the exact disjunction of the two assertions above it, so it could only ever duplicate a message; the first repair replaced it with an errors.Is disjunction that was dead in the same way.
records.evidence: With the legs broken asymmetrically, deleting the block left the test failing identically.
records.reason: Deleted. The two errors.Is assertions above it already pin the sentinel.

records.finding: The race test flagged only a total silent drop, while partial drops are a real mode of the bug.
records.evidence: Re-review classifier against the broken code: 119 partial per 2000 against 50 fully silent.
records.reason: The assertion requires the full batch. Its justification was itself corrected afterwards: in this test's one-chunk shape every observed detection is total, and the comment now says so rather than claiming partial is common there.

records.finding: The Shutdown doc leaned the trade-off on a retry the only in-tree caller cannot perform, and dropped the sentence naming the goroutine leak without replacing it.
records.evidence: emit.Std.Close is sync.Once-guarded and caches closeErr; a direct retry also returns non-nil because otlpmetrichttp's shutdownOnce errors on the second call.
records.reason: The doc states the retry limitation, the leak, and which failure is the cheaper one.

records.finding: Across rounds the Shutdown comment first misattributed the cost of holding the slot, then had its justification deleted while the defer stayed, leaving a reader unable to tell whether the hold was load-bearing.
records.evidence: Reviewer proved by mutation that releasing before the stop is behaviourally equivalent for the stated guarantee, surviving 6/6 runs.
records.reason: Restored as what it is: a latency choice, not a correctness dependency, with the ordering argument stated as the thing that carries the guarantee.

records.finding: Three comments still named providerSink.mu after the rewrite deleted it, one of them in the doc of the very test the rewrite changed.
records.evidence: grep for providerSink.mu after the change.
records.reason: All three rewritten; no stale references remain.

records.finding: TestShutdownHonorsItsDeadline ordered itself with a 20ms sleep; if the emit had not taken the slot in time the test would fail on a misleading assertion.
records.evidence: Reviewer saw zero failures in 190 runs including under 8-way load, but the ordering was a sleep, not a synchronisation.
records.reason: It gates on the exporter actually entering Export.

records.finding: Both error branches in resolveResource were provably unreachable, and the comment said so about one of them while the code still handled it.
records.evidence: resource.Merge never returns nil for two non-nil arguments, and Environment() is always schemaless so ErrSchemaURLConflict cannot fire.
records.reason: The nil fallback is gone; the error handler stays with a comment saying it is unreachable today and why it is kept.

records.finding: The change made the conformance harness the only Exporter construction not resolving its resource, so the suite ran a shape production no longer builds.
records.evidence: New and newWith route through resolveResource; the harness built the struct literal with a raw defaultResource().
records.reason: The harness resolves too. Noted honestly: no assertion covers this, because the suite counts records and never inspects the resource.

records.finding: This change makes otlp the only exporter for which Shutdown is terminal, and emit.Exporter's contract is silent on post-Shutdown exports while three siblings keep working.
records.evidence: emit/emit.go's Exporter doc names only batching, flush on Shutdown and capability honesty; testkit/conformance has no post-Shutdown invariant.
records.reason: REFUTED by the cross-examiner. Nothing is made false — docs-accuracy's shapes are all about a claim contradicted or left stale, and the finding concedes no sentence is now false. portability.md 6.5 already binds every implementation to never lose events without a visible counter; this change moves otlp into compliance with that uniform rule rather than inventing an adapter-local contract. The interface question is tracked on its own item.

records.finding: The ErrShutdown doc says emit.Std.Flush turns it into biz_dropped_events_total{reason=export}, but in that state the metric leg is also down so the counter point can never ship.
records.evidence: End-to-end run: no such point reached the backend; the outcome is a warning plus an in-memory counter.
records.reason: REFUTED. The sentence claims the increment, which emit/emitter.go does perform, and makes no delivery claim. emit.Std.Close already documents the terminal limit honestly.

records.finding: 'resolveResource is the single place a resource becomes the one both legs carry' understates a second Environment() parse inside sdklog.WithResource, which doubles otel.Handle warnings on malformed input.
records.evidence: Counting handler: 2 calls per New for a single-error value.
records.reason: REFUTED. The very next sentence of the same comment discloses that sdklog.WithResource merges Environment() into whatever it is given, the second merge is a verified no-op, and the measurement in the finding was off.

records.finding: Routing OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES onto the metric resource was said to conflict with ADR-0004's events-only rule, since a Collector can promote resource attributes to metric labels.
records.evidence: ADR-0004: 'biz.entity.id and biz.customer.id are events-only attributes ... the emit layer's label construction makes it structurally impossible'.
records.reason: REFUTED. The rule is scoped to two named keys and to LABEL construction; resource attributes are not metric labels, the metric resource already carries per-process identity by design, and those attributes already reached the event resource before this change. The finding itself concedes it is not a cardinality defect.
